import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll, afterAll, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';
import { HttpException, NotFoundException, BadRequestException } from '@nestjs/common';
import { WritesService } from '../src/writes/writes.service.js';
import { OperationsService } from '../src/operations/operations.service.js';
import { OperationsRepository } from '../src/operations/operations.repository.js';
import { ProjectionsService } from '../src/projections/projections.service.js';
import { ProjectionsRepository } from '../src/projections/projections.repository.js';
import type { CreateOrderInput, OperationRow, CompanyTotals } from '../src/projections/projections.types.js';

let prisma: PrismaClient;
let writesService: WritesService;
let operationsService: OperationsService;
let projectionsService: ProjectionsService;

// --- helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------

async function cleanAll(): Promise<void> {
  await prisma.operationReadModel.deleteMany({});
  await prisma.companyFinancialTotal.deleteMany({});
  await prisma.paymentOrder.deleteMany({});
  await prisma.worker.deleteMany({});
  await prisma.event.deleteMany({});
}

async function makeWorker(name: string, companyId: string): Promise<string> {
  const w = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { name, companyId } });
  return w.id;
}

async function makeEvent(title: string, location: string): Promise<string> {
  const e = await prisma.event.create({ data: { title, location } });
  return e.id;
}

function makeOrderInput(overrides: Partial<CreateOrderInput> = {}): CreateOrderInput {
  return {
    companyId: 'company-a',
    workerId: 'worker-1',
    eventId: 'event-1',
    amountCents: 5000,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

async function createAndVerifyOrder(
  companyId: string,
  workerId: string,
  eventId: string,
  amountCents: number,
): Promise<string> {
  const result = await writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId, eventId, amountCents });
  return result.id;
}

function getErrorEnvelope(ex: unknown): { code: string; message: string; details: Record<string, unknown> } {
  if (ex instanceof HttpException) {
    const resp = ex.getResponse();
    if (typeof resp === 'object' && resp !== null) {
      const body = resp as Record<string, unknown>;
      const error = body.error as { code: string; message: string; details: Record<string, unknown> };
      return error;
    }
  }
  throw new Error(`Expected HttpException with envelope, got: ${ex instanceof Error ? ex.message : String(ex)}`);
}

// --- setup / teardown -------------------------------------------------------

beforeAll(async () => {
  prisma = new PrismaClient();
  const projectionsRepo = new ProjectionsRepository(prisma);
  projectionsService = new ProjectionsService(projectionsRepo);
  writesService = new WritesService(prisma, projectionsService);
  const operationsRepo = new OperationsRepository(prisma);
  operationsService = new OperationsService(operationsRepo);
});

afterAll(async () => {
  await prisma.$disconnect();
});

beforeEach(async () => {
  await cleanAll();
});

// --- 1. Read-your-own-writes: create order ----------------------------------

describe('read-your-own-writes', () => {
  it('create order then immediately query the dashboard for that company — the new row appears with correct denormalised fields', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-a';
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Alice', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Conference', 'Hall A');

    const orderId = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, 12000);

    const page = await operationsService.query({ companyId, page: 1, pageSize: 10 });

    expect(page.total).toBe(1);
    expect(page.items).toHaveLength(1);
    const row = page.items[0];
    expect(row.id).toBe(orderId);
    expect(row.companyId).toBe(companyId);
    expect(row.workerId).toBe(workerId);
    expect(row.workerName).toBe('Alice');
    expect(row.eventId).toBe(eventId);
    expect(row.eventTitle).toBe('Conference');
    expect(row.eventLocation).toBe('Hall A');
    expect(row.status).toBe('pending');
    expect(row.amountCents).toBe(12000);
  });

  it('approve an order then query filtered by status=approved — the row appears under approved', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-a';
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Bob', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Workshop', 'Room 2');

    const orderId = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, 7500);
    await writesService.approveOrder(orderId);

    const page = await operationsService.query({ companyId, status: 'approved', page: 1, pageSize: 10 });
    expect(page.total).toBe(1);
    expect(page.items[0].id).toBe(orderId);
    expect(page.items[0].status).toBe('approved');
  });

  it('reject an order then query filtered by status=rejected — the row appears under rejected and is absent from approved', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-a';
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Carol', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Seminar', 'Room 3');

    const orderId = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, 3000);
    await writesService.rejectOrder(orderId);

    const rejectedPage = await operationsService.query({ companyId, status: 'rejected', page: 1, pageSize: 10 });
    expect(rejectedPage.total).toBe(1);
    expect(rejectedPage.items[0].id).toBe(orderId);
    expect(rejectedPage.items[0].status).toBe('rejected');

    const approvedPage = await operationsService.query({ companyId, status: 'approved', page: 1, pageSize: 10 });
    expect(approvedPage.total).toBe(0);
  });
});

// --- 2. Concurrency ----------------------------------------------------------

describe('concurrent updates', () => {
  it('10 concurrent approveOrder calls on distinct orders for the same company produce exact totals', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-concurrent';
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Dave', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Meetup', 'Lobby');

    const amounts: number[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
      const amt = (i + 1) * 1000;
      amounts.push(amt);
      await writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId, eventId, amountCents: amt });
    }

    const orders = await prisma.paymentOrder.findMany({ where: { companyId } });
    const orderIds = orders.map((o) => o.id);

    await Promise.all(orderIds.map((id) => writesService.approveOrder(id)));

    const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
    expect(totals).not.toBeNull();
    const expectedApproved = amounts.reduce((sum, a) => sum + BigInt(a), 0n);
    expect(totals!.approvedTotalCents).toBe(expectedApproved);
    expect(totals!.rejectedTotalCents).toBe(0n);
    expect(totals!.pendingCount).toBe(0);
  });

  it('concurrent createOrder and approveOrder interleaved for one company preserve totals invariant', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-mixed';
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Eve', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Hackathon', 'Lab');

    // Create 5 orders that will be approved
    const approveAmounts: number[] = [];
    const approveOrderIds: string[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      const amt = (i + 1) * 2000;
      approveAmounts.push(amt);
      const id = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, amt);
      approveOrderIds.push(id);
    }

    // Create 5 orders that will remain pending
    const pendingAmounts: number[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      const amt = (i + 1) * 3000;
      pendingAmounts.push(amt);
      await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, amt);
    }

    // Fire approves concurrently (creates are already done, so no create/approve race here;
    // but we still test concurrent approve + a concurrent new create)
    const newCreatePromise = writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId, eventId, amountCents: 9999 });
    const approvePromises = approveOrderIds.map((id) => writesService.approveOrder(id));

    await Promise.all([newCreatePromise, ...approvePromises]);

    const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
    expect(totals).not.toBeNull();
    const expectedApproved = approveAmounts.reduce((sum, a) => sum + BigInt(a), 0n);
    expect(totals!.approvedTotalCents).toBe(expectedApproved);
    // 5 pending originals + 1 new = 6 pending
    expect(totals!.pendingCount).toBe(6);
    expect(totals!.rejectedTotalCents).toBe(0n);
  });
});

// --- 3. Drift repair ---------------------------------------------------------

describe('drift repair', () => {
  it('corrupt a projection row (status + amount), run repairDrift — projection matches source and totals are corrected', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-drift1';
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Frank', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Retreat', 'Venue B');

    const orderId = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, 8000);

    // Corrupt: change status to 'approved' and amount to 9999 in the projection
    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE operation_read_models
      SET status = 'approved', amount_cents = 9999
      WHERE id = ${orderId}
    `;

    const from = new Date(Date.now() - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
    const to = new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);

    const report = await projectionsService.repairDrift(from, to);
    expect(report.rowsCorrected).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);

    // Verify projection now matches source
    const row = await prisma.operationReadModel.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: orderId } });
    expect(row.status).toBe('pending');
    expect(row.amountCents).toBe(8000);

    // Verify totals are corrected (should be pending_count=1, approved=0)
    const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
    expect(totals).not.toBeNull();
    expect(totals!.pendingCount).toBe(1);
    expect(totals!.approvedTotalCents).toBe(0n);
  });

  it('delete a projection row, run repairDrift — the row is restored with correct fields and totals include its contribution', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-drift2';
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Grace', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Symposium', 'Center');

    const orderId = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, 4500);

    // Delete the projection row directly
    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      DELETE FROM operation_read_models WHERE id = ${orderId}
    `;

    const from = new Date(Date.now() - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
    const to = new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);

    const report = await projectionsService.repairDrift(from, to);
    expect(report.rowsCorrected).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);

    // Verify row is restored
    const row = await prisma.operationReadModel.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: orderId } });
    expect(row.companyId).toBe(companyId);
    expect(row.workerName).toBe('Grace');
    expect(row.eventTitle).toBe('Symposium');
    expect(row.status).toBe('pending');
    expect(row.amountCents).toBe(4500);

    // Totals should reflect the restored row
    const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
    expect(totals).not.toBeNull();
    expect(totals!.pendingCount).toBe(1);
  });

  it('run repairDrift for a window that contains no orders — returns rowsCorrected=0 and totalsCorrected=false', async () => {
    const from = new Date('2020-01-01T00:00:00Z');
    const to = new Date('2020-01-02T00:00:00Z');

    const report = await projectionsService.repairDrift(from, to);
    expect(report.rowsCorrected).toBe(0);
    expect(report.totalsCorrected).toBe(false);
  });
});

// --- 4. Re-derivation ---------------------------------------------------------

describe('re-derivation', () => {
  it('create orders, corrupt projection, run rederive — projection matches source and totals are recomputed', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-rederive';
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Heidi', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Forum', 'Stage');

    const order1 = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, 1000);
    const order2 = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, 2000);
    const order3 = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, 3000);

    // Approve order1
    await writesService.approveOrder(order1);

    // Corrupt: wrong status on order2, wrong amount on order3
    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE operation_read_models SET status = 'approved' WHERE id = ${order2}
    `;
    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE operation_read_models SET amount_cents = 99999 WHERE id = ${order3}
    `;

    const from = new Date(Date.now() - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
    const to = new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);

    const report = await projectionsService.rederive(from, to);
    expect(report.rowsCorrected).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);

    // Verify all three rows match source
    const r1 = await prisma.operationReadModel.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: order1 } });
    expect(r1.status).toBe('approved');
    expect(r1.amountCents).toBe(1000);

    const r2 = await prisma.operationReadModel.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: order2 } });
    expect(r2.status).toBe('pending');
    expect(r2.amountCents).toBe(2000);

    const r3 = await prisma.operationReadModel.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: order3 } });
    expect(r3.status).toBe('pending');
    expect(r3.amountCents).toBe(3000);

    // Totals: 1 approved (1000), 2 pending
    const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
    expect(totals).not.toBeNull();
    expect(totals!.approvedTotalCents).toBe(1000n);
    expect(totals!.pendingCount).toBe(2);
  });
});

describe('pagination', () => {
  async function seedCompany(companyId: string, count: number): Promise<void> {
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Pagination Worker', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Pag Event', 'Loc');
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      await writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId, eventId, amountCents: 100 + i });
    }
  }

  it('insert 25 rows, query page 1 size 10 — returns exactly 10 items and total is 25', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-pag1';
    await seedCompany(companyId, 25);

    const page = await operationsService.query({ companyId, page: 1, pageSize: 10 });
    expect(page.items).toHaveLength(10);
    expect(page.total).toBe(25);
    expect(page.page).toBe(1);
    expect(page.pageSize).toBe(10);
  });

  it('query page 3 size 10 for a company with 25 rows — returns exactly 5 items', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-pag3';
    await seedCompany(companyId, 25);

    const page = await operationsService.query({ companyId, page: 3, pageSize: 10 });
    expect(page.items).toHaveLength(5);
    expect(page.total).toBe(25);
  });

  it('query page 99 size 10 for a company with 25 rows — returns 0 items and total is still 25', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-pag99';
    await seedCompany(companyId, 25);

    const page = await operationsService.query({ companyId, page: 99, pageSize: 10 });
    expect(page.items).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(page.total).toBe(25);
  });
});

// --- 6. Date range filtering ----------------------------------------------------

describe('date range filtering', () => {
  it('only strictly-in-range rows are returned; from is included, to is excluded', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-daterange';
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Date Worker', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Date Event', 'DateLoc');

    // We'll create 3 orders and then overwrite their created_at in both source and projection
    const orderBefore = await writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId, eventId, amountCents: 100 });
    const orderIn = await writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId, eventId, amountCents: 200 });
    const orderAtFrom = await writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId, eventId, amountCents: 300 });
    const orderAtTo = await writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId, eventId, amountCents: 400 });

    const from = new Date('2025-06-01T00:00:00.000Z');
    const to = new Date('2025-06-05T00:00:00.000Z');

    // Set created_at on source and projection
    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE payment_orders SET created_at = '2025-05-30T00:00:00.000Z' WHERE id = ${orderBefore.id}
    `;
    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE operation_read_models SET created_at = '2025-05-30T00:00:00.000Z' WHERE id = ${orderBefore.id}
    `;

    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE payment_orders SET created_at = '2025-06-02T00:00:00.000Z' WHERE id = ${orderIn.id}
    `;
    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE operation_read_models SET created_at = '2025-06-02T00:00:00.000Z' WHERE id = ${orderIn.id}
    `;

    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE payment_orders SET created_at = '2025-06-01T00:00:00.000Z' WHERE id = ${orderAtFrom.id}
    `;
    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE operation_read_models SET created_at = '2025-06-01T00:00:00.000Z' WHERE id = ${orderAtFrom.id}
    `;

    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE payment_orders SET created_at = '2025-06-05T00:00:00.000Z' WHERE id = ${orderAtTo.id}
    `;
    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE operation_read_models SET created_at = '2025-06-05T00:00:00.000Z' WHERE id = ${orderAtTo.id}
    `;

    const page = await operationsService.query({ companyId, from, to, page: 1, pageSize: 100 });
    const ids = page.items.map((r) => r.id);
    expect(page.total).toBe(2);
    expect(ids).toContain(orderAtFrom.id); // from is included (gte)
    expect(ids).toContain(orderIn.id);
    expect(ids).not.toContain(orderBefore.id); // before from
    expect(ids).not.toContain(orderAtTo.id); // to is excluded (lt)
  });
});

describe('error handling', () => {
  it('approveOrder with a non-existent UUID — returns an error with code order_not_found', async () => {
    // ASSUMPTION: WritesService throws exceptions carrying the standard error envelope (code/message/details) in the HttpException response, consistent with OperationsService and the plan's error contract.
    await expect(writesService.approveOrder('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000')).rejects.toThrow();

    try {
      await writesService.approveOrder('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000');
    } catch (ex) {
      const envelope = getErrorEnvelope(ex);
      expect(envelope.code).toBe('order_not_found');
    }
  });

  it('approveOrder on an already-approved order — returns an error with code invalid_transition', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-err';
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Err Worker', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Err Event', 'ErrLoc');

    const orderId = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, 1000);
    await writesService.approveOrder(orderId);

    // ASSUMPTION: same envelope pattern as above
    try {
      await writesService.approveOrder(orderId);
      expect.fail('should have thrown');
    } catch (ex) {
      const envelope = getErrorEnvelope(ex);
      expect(envelope.code).toBe('invalid_transition');
    }
  });

  it('dashboard with pageSize=101 — returns an error with code invalid_query_params', async () => {
    try {
      await operationsService.query({ companyId: 'x', page: 1, pageSize: 101 });
      expect.fail('should have thrown');
    } catch (ex) {
      const envelope = getErrorEnvelope(ex);
      expect(envelope.code).toBe('invalid_query_params');
    }
  });

  it('dashboard with page=0 — returns an error with code invalid_query_params', async () => {
    try {
      await operationsService.query({ companyId: 'x', page: 0, pageSize: 10 });
      expect.fail('should have thrown');
    } catch (ex) {
      const envelope = getErrorEnvelope(ex);
      expect(envelope.code).toBe('invalid_query_params');
    }
  });
});

describe('sort stability', () => {
  it('two orders with identical created_at — both appear and relative order is stable across repeated queries', async () => {
    const companyId = 'company-stable';
    const workerId = await makeWorker('Stable Worker', companyId);
    const eventId = await makeEvent('Stable Event', 'StableLoc');

    const order1 = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, 1000);
    const order2 = await createAndVerifyOrder(companyId, workerId, eventId, 2000);

    // Set both to the same timestamp
    const fixedDate = new Date('2025-07-01T12:00:00.000Z');
    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE payment_orders SET created_at = ${fixedDate} WHERE id IN (${order1.id}, ${order2.id})
    `;
    await prisma.$executeRaw`
      UPDATE operation_read_models SET created_at = ${fixedDate} WHERE id IN (${order1.id}, ${order2.id})
    `;

    const page1 = await operationsService.query({ companyId, page: 1, pageSize: 10 });
    const page2 = await operationsService.query({ companyId, page: 1, pageSize: 10 });

    expect(page1.items).toHaveLength(2);
    const ids1 = page1.items.map((r) => r.id);
    const ids2 = page2.items.map((r) => r.id);

    // Both orders must appear
    expect(ids1).toContain(order1.id);
    expect(ids1).toContain(order2.id);

    // Relative order must be stable
    expect(ids1).toEqual(ids2);
  });
});

it('fire concurrent createOrder and approveOrder interleaved for one company — final totals match', async () => {
  const companyId = randomUUID();
  const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Eve' } });
  const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Fair', location: 'Grounds' } });

  // Create 5 orders that will be approved
  const toApprove = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId: worker.id, eventId: event.id, amountCents: 100 * (i + 1) });
    toApprove.push({ id, amount: 100 * (i + 1) });
  }

  // Now fire concurrent: 5 new creates + 5 approves on existing
  const results = await Promise.all([
    ...toApprove.map((o) => writesService.approveOrder(o.id)),
    ...Array.from({ length: 5 }, (_, i) =>
      writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId: worker.id, eventId: event.id, amountCents: 500 * (i + 1) }),
    ),
  ]);

  // Final state: 5 approved, 5 pending
  const totalApprovedCents = toApprove.reduce((sum, o) => sum + BigInt(o.amount), 0n);
  const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
  expect(totals.approvedTotalCents).toBe(totalApprovedCents);
  expect(totals.pendingCount).toBe(5);
});
```

**Case 6: Corrupt projection row, run repairDrift**
```ts
it('corrupt a projection row then run repairDrift — projection matches source and totals are corrected', async () => {
  const companyId = randomUUID();
  const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Frank' } });
  const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Mixer', location: 'Lobby' } });

  const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId: worker.id, eventId: event.id, amountCents: 750 });
  
  // Approve it first
  await writesService.approveOrder(id);

  // Now corrupt the projection row directly
  const sourceOrder = await prisma.paymentOrder.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id } });
  const windowStart = new Date(sourceOrder.createdAt.getTime() - 1000);
  const windowEnd = new Date(sourceOrder.createdAt.getTime() + 1000);

  await prisma.operationReadModel.update({
    where: { id },
    data: { status: 'rejected', amountCents: 9999 },
  });

  await projectionsService.repairDrift(windowStart, windowEnd);

  const repaired = await prisma.operationReadModel.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id } });
  expect(repaired.status).toBe('approved');
  expect(repaired.amountCents).toBe(750);

  const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
  expect(totals.approvedTotalCents).toBe(750n);
  expect(totals.rejectedTotalCents).toBe(0n);
  expect(totals.pendingCount).toBe(0);
});
```

**Case 7: Delete projection row, run repairDrift**
```ts
it('delete a projection row then run repairDrift — row is restored and totals include its contribution', async () => {
  const companyId = randomUUID();
  const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Grace' } });
  const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Talk', location: 'Room A' } });

  const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId: worker.id, eventId: event.id, amountCents: 420 });

  const sourceOrder = await prisma.paymentOrder.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id } });
  const windowStart = new Date(sourceOrder.createdAt.getTime() - 1000);
  const windowEnd = new Date(sourceOrder.createdAt.getTime() + 1000);

  // Delete the projection row
  await prisma.operationReadModel.delete({ where: { id } });

  // Reset totals to zero (simulating the drift)
  await prisma.companyFinancialTotal.update({ where: { companyId }, data: { pendingCount: 0 } });

  await projectionsService.repairDrift(windowStart, windowEnd);

  const restored = await prisma.operationReadModel.findUnique({ where: { id } });
  expect(restored).not.toBeNull();
  expect(restored!.status).toBe('pending');
  expect(restored!.amountCents).toBe(420);

  const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
  expect(totals.pendingCount).toBe(1);
});
```

**Case 8: Re-derivation after corruption**
```ts
it('create orders, corrupt projection, run rederive — projection is rebuilt from source', async () => {
  const companyId = randomUUID();
  const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Hank' } });
  const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Demo', location: 'Stage' } });

  const amounts = [100, 200, 300];
  const orderIds = [];
  for (const amount of amounts) {
    const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({ companyId, workerId: worker.id, eventId: event.id, amountCents: amount });
    orderIds.push(id);
  }

  // Approve the first one
  await writesService.approveOrder(orderIds[0]);

  // Corrupt: wrong status on second, wrong amount on third
  await prisma.operationReadModel.update({ where: { id: orderIds[1] }, data: { status: 'approved' } });
  await prisma.operationReadModel.update({ where: { id: orderIds[2] }, data: { amountCents: 99999 } });

  const sourceOrders = await prisma.paymentOrder.findMany({ where: { companyId } });
  const minDate = new Date(Math.min(...sourceOrders.map((o) => o.createdAt.getTime())) - 1000);
  const maxDate = new Date(Math.max(...sourceOrders.map((o) => o.createdAt.getTime())) + 1000);

  await projectionsService.rederive(minDate, maxDate);

  // Verify all rows match source
  for (const orderId of orderIds) {
    const source = await prisma.paymentOrder.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: orderId } });
    const projection = await prisma.operationReadModel.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: orderId } });
    expect(projection.status).toBe(source.status);
    expect(projection.amountCents).toBe(source.amountCents);
  }

  // Verify totals: 1 approved (100), 2 pending
  const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
  expect(totals.approvedTotalCents).toBe(100n);
  expect(totals.pendingCount).toBe(2);
});
```

```ts
it('query with date range — row at from is included, row at to is excluded', async () => {
  const companyId = randomUUID();
  const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Leo' } });
  const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Seminar', location: 'Auditorium' } });

  // We need to create orders with specific timestamps. Since WritesService doesn't accept createdAt,
  // we'll insert directly into payment_orders and manually create projection rows.
  
  const baseTime = new Date('2024-06-15T12:00:00.000Z');
  const beforeFrom = new Date(baseTime.getTime() - 60000); // 1 min before
  const atFrom = new Date(baseTime); // exactly at from
  const inRange = new Date(baseTime.getTime() + 30000); // 30s after from
  const atTo = new Date(baseTime.getTime() + 60000); // exactly at to (should be excluded)
  const afterTo = new Date(baseTime.getTime() + 120000); // 2 min after

  const orders = [
    { id: randomUUID(), createdAt: beforeFrom, amountCents: 10 },
    { id: randomUUID(), createdAt: atFrom, amountCents: 20 },
    { id: randomUUID(), createdAt: inRange, amountCents: 30 },
    { id: randomUUID(), createdAt: atTo, amountCents: 40 },
    { id: randomUUID(), createdAt: afterTo, amountCents: 50 },
  ];

  for (const o of orders) {
    await prisma.paymentOrder.create({
      data: {
        id: o.id,
        companyId,
        workerId: worker.id,
        eventId: event.id,
        amountCents: o.amountCents,
        createdAt: o.createdAt,
      },
    });
    // Manually create projection row
    await prisma.operationReadModel.create({
      data: {
        id: o.id,
        companyId,
        workerId: worker.id,
        workerName: worker.name,
        eventId: event.id,
        eventTitle: event.title,
        eventLocation: event.location,
        status: 'pending',
        amountCents: o.amountCents,
        createdAt: o.createdAt,
      },
    });
  }

  const page = await operationsService.query({
    companyId,
    from: baseTime,
    to: new Date(baseTime.getTime() + 60000), // atTo
    page: 1,
    pageSize: 10,
  });

  const returnedIds = page.items.map((r) => r.id);
  expect(returnedIds).toContain(atFrom order id);
  expect(returnedIds).toContain(inRange order id);
  expect(returnedIds).not.toContain(beforeFrom order id);
  expect(returnedIds).not.toContain(atTo order id);
  expect(returnedIds).not.toContain(afterTo order id);
  expect(page.total).toBe(2);
});
```

In NestJS, `new BadRequestException(response)` sets the response body to `response`. The `exception.response` or `exception.getResponse()` returns it. So if I throw `new BadRequestException({ error: { code: 'invalid_query_params', ... } })`, then `exception.response` should be `{ error: { code: 'invalid_query_params', ... } }`.

} catch (e) {

import { describe, it, beforeAll, afterAll, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';
import { BadRequestException, NotFoundException } from '@nestjs/common';
import { OperationsService } from '../src/operations/operations.service.js';
import { OperationsRepository } from '../src/operations/operations.repository.js';
import { ProjectionsService } from '../src/projections/projections.service.js';
import { ProjectionsRepository } from '../src/projections/projections.repository.js';
import { WritesService } from '../src/writes/writes.service.js';

describe('Operations (integration)', () => {
  let prisma: PrismaClient;
  let operationsService: OperationsService;
  let projectionsService: ProjectionsService;
  let writesService: WritesService;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    prisma = new PrismaClient();
    const projectionsRepo = new ProjectionsRepository(prisma);
    projectionsService = new ProjectionsService(projectionsRepo);
    const operationsRepo = new OperationsRepository(prisma);
    operationsService = new OperationsService(operationsRepo);
    writesService = new WritesService(prisma, projectionsService);
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    await prisma.$disconnect();
  });

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await prisma.operationReadModel.deleteMany({});
    await prisma.companyFinancialTotal.deleteMany({});
    await prisma.paymentOrder.deleteMany({});
    await prisma.worker.deleteMany({});
    await prisma.event.deleteMany({});
  });

  // ─── Read-your-own-writes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

  describe('read-your-own-writes', () => {
    it('create order then immediately query the dashboard — new row appears with correct denormalised fields', async () => {
      const companyId = randomUUID();
      const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Alice' } });
      const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Concert', location: 'Arena' } });

      const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({
        companyId,
        workerId: worker.id,
        eventId: event.id,
        amountCents: 5000,
      });

      const page = await operationsService.query({ companyId, page: 1, pageSize: 10 });

      expect(page.total).toBe(1);
      expect(page.items[0].id).toBe(id);
      expect(page.items[0].companyId).toBe(companyId);
      expect(page.items[0].workerName).toBe('Alice');
      expect(page.items[0].eventTitle).toBe('Concert');
      expect(page.items[0].eventLocation).toBe('Arena');
      expect(page.items[0].status).toBe('pending');
      expect(page.items[0].amountCents).toBe(5000);
    });

    it('approve an order then query filtered by status=approved — row status reflects the transition', async () => {
      const companyId = randomUUID();
      const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Bob' } });
      const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Festival', location: 'Park' } });

      const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({
        companyId,
        workerId: worker.id,
        eventId: event.id,
        amountCents: 3000,
      });
      await writesService.approveOrder(id);

      const page = await operationsService.query({ companyId, status: 'approved', page: 1, pageSize: 10 });

      expect(page.total).toBe(1);
      expect(page.items[0].id).toBe(id);
      expect(page.items[0].status).toBe('approved');
    });

    it('reject an order then query filtered by status=rejected — row appears under rejected and is absent from approved', async () => {
      const companyId = randomUUID();
      const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Carol' } });
      const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Show', location: 'Theater' } });

      const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({
        companyId,
        workerId: worker.id,
        eventId: event.id,
        amountCents: 2000,
      });
      await writesService.rejectOrder(id);

      const rejectedPage = await operationsService.query({ companyId, status: 'rejected', page: 1, pageSize: 10 });
      expect(rejectedPage.total).toBe(1);
      expect(rejectedPage.items[0].id).toBe(id);
      expect(rejectedPage.items[0].status).toBe('rejected');

      const approvedPage = await operationsService.query({ companyId, status: 'approved', page: 1, pageSize: 10 });
      expect(approvedPage.total).toBe(0);
    });
  });

  // ─── Concurrent updates ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  describe('concurrent updates', () => {
    it('fire 10 concurrent approveOrder calls on distinct orders for the same company — totals are exact', async () => {
      const companyId = randomUUID();
      const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Dave' } });
      const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Gala', location: 'Hall' } });

      const amounts = [100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, 1000];
      const orderIds: string[] = [];
      for (const amount of amounts) {
        const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({
          companyId,
          workerId: worker.id,
          eventId: event.id,
          amountCents: amount,
        });
        orderIds.push(id);
      }

      await Promise.all(orderIds.map((id) => writesService.approveOrder(id)));

      const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
      expect(totals.approvedTotalCents).toBe(5500n);
      expect(totals.pendingCount).toBe(0);
    });

    it('fire concurrent createOrder and approveOrder interleaved for one company — final totals match', async () => {
      const companyId = randomUUID();
      const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Eve' } });
      const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Fair', location: 'Grounds' } });

      const toApprove: { id: string; amount: number }[] = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
        const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({
          companyId,
          workerId: worker.id,
          eventId: event.id,
          amountCents: 100 * (i + 1),
        });
        toApprove.push({ id, amount: 100 * (i + 1) });
      }

      await Promise.all([
        ...toApprove.map((o) => writesService.approveOrder(o.id)),
        ...Array.from({ length: 5 }, (_, i) =>
          writesService.createOrder({
            companyId,
            workerId: worker.id,
            eventId: event.id,
            amountCents: 500 * (i + 1),
          }),
        ),
      ]);

      const expectedApproved = toApprove.reduce((sum, o) => sum + BigInt(o.amount), 0n);
      const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
      expect(totals.approvedTotalCents).toBe(expectedApproved);
      expect(totals.pendingCount).toBe(5);
    });
  });

  // ─── Drift repair ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  describe('drift repair', () => {
    it('corrupt a projection row (status + amount) then run repairDrift — projection matches source and totals are corrected', async () => {
      const companyId = randomUUID();
      const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Frank' } });
      const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Mixer', location: 'Lobby' } });

      const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({
        companyId,
        workerId: worker.id,
        eventId: event.id,
        amountCents: 750,
      });
      await writesService.approveOrder(id);

      const sourceOrder = await prisma.paymentOrder.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id } });
      const windowStart = new Date(sourceOrder.createdAt.getTime() - 1000);
      const windowEnd = new Date(sourceOrder.createdAt.getTime() + 1000);

      await prisma.operationReadModel.update({
        where: { id },
        data: { status: 'rejected', amountCents: 9999 },
      });

      await projectionsService.repairDrift(windowStart, windowEnd);

      const repaired = await prisma.operationReadModel.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id } });
      expect(repaired.status).toBe('approved');
      expect(repaired.amountCents).toBe(750);

      const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
      expect(totals.approvedTotalCents).toBe(750n);
      expect(totals.rejectedTotalCents).toBe(0n);
      expect(totals.pendingCount).toBe(0);
    });

    it('delete a projection row then run repairDrift — row is restored and totals include its contribution', async () => {
      const companyId = randomUUID();
      const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Grace' } });
      const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Talk', location: 'Room A' } });

      const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({
        companyId,
        workerId: worker.id,
        eventId: event.id,
        amountCents: 420,
      });

      const sourceOrder = await prisma.paymentOrder.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id } });
      const windowStart = new Date(sourceOrder.createdAt.getTime() - 1000);
      const windowEnd = new Date(sourceOrder.createdAt.getTime() + 1000);

      await prisma.operationReadModel.delete({ where: { id } });
      await prisma.companyFinancialTotal.update({
        where: { companyId },
        data: { pendingCount: 0 },
      });

      await projectionsService.repairDrift(windowStart, windowEnd);

      const restored = await prisma.operationReadModel.findUnique({ where: { id } });
      expect(restored).not.toBeNull();
      expect(restored!.status).toBe('pending');
      expect(restored!.amountCents).toBe(420);

      const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
      expect(totals.pendingCount).toBe(1);
    });

    it('run repairDrift for a window that contains no orders — returns rowsCorrected=0 and totalsCorrected=false', async () => {
      const windowStart = new Date('2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z');
      const windowEnd = new Date('2020-01-02T00:00:00.000Z');

      const report = await projectionsService.repairDrift(windowStart, windowEnd);
      expect(report.rowsCorrected).toBe(0);
      expect(report.totalsCorrected).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  // ─── Re-derivation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  describe('re-derivation', () => {
    it('create orders, corrupt projection, run rederive — projection is rebuilt from source and totals are recomputed', async () => {
      const companyId = randomUUID();
      const worker = await prisma.worker.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), companyId, name: 'Hank' } });
      const event = await prisma.event.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), title: 'Demo', location: 'Stage' } });

      const orderIds: string[] = [];
      for (const amount of [100, 200, 300]) {
        const { id } = await writesService.createOrder({
          companyId,
          workerId: worker.id,
          eventId: event.id,
          amountCents: amount,
        });
        orderIds.push(id);
      }

      await writesService.approveOrder(orderIds[0]);

      // Corrupt: wrong status on second, wrong amount on third
      await prisma.operationReadModel.update({ where: { id: orderIds[1] }, data: { status: 'approved' } });
      await prisma.operationReadModel.update({ where: { id: orderIds[2] }, data: { amountCents: 99999 } });

      const sourceOrders = await prisma.paymentOrder.findMany({ where: { companyId } });
      const minDate = new Date(Math.min(...sourceOrders.map((o) => o.createdAt.getTime())) - 1000);
      const maxDate = new Date(Math.max(...sourceOrders.map((o) => o.createdAt.getTime())) + 1000);

      await projectionsService.rederive(minDate, maxDate);

      for (const orderId of orderIds) {
        const source = await prisma.paymentOrder.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: orderId } });
        const projection = await prisma.operationReadModel.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: orderId } });
        expect(projection.status).toBe(source.status);
        expect(projection.amountCents).toBe(source.amountCents);
      }

      const totals = await projectionsService.getTotals(companyId);
      expect(totals.approvedTotalCents).toBe(100n);
      expect(totals.pendingCount).toBe(2);
    });
  });

            id: o.id,

            eventLocation: event.location,
            status: 'pending',
            amountCents: o.amountCents,
            createdAt: o.createdAt,
          },
        });
      }

      const page = await operationsService.query({ companyId, from, to, page: 1, pageSize: 10 });

      const returnedIds = page.items.map((r) => r.id);
      expect(returnedIds).toContain(orders[1].id); // at from — included
      expect(returnedIds).toContain(orders[2].id); // in range — included
      expect(returnedIds).not.toContain(orders[0].id); // before from — excluded

# DESIGN.md

## Problem
- dashboard operations list join of payment orders, events, workers filtered by company/status/date sorted recency paginated. 3M orders -> 20-30s.
- requirements: p95 <50ms, read-your-writes immediate, exact financial totals per company.

## Chosen approach
- synchronous application-managed read models maintained in same DB transaction as source writes.
- two read tables: per-order operation rows denormalized; per-company financial totals.
- write path: source write + projection upsert/status + totals adjust atomically. Reads only projection tables.
- rebuild tools: re-derive window, scheduled drift repair, manual trigger.

## Why this meets requirements
- read latency: single table indexed query no multi-table join, index supports filters/sort; count from projection.
- read-your-writes: committed source and projection together; next request sees both. No async lag/cache invalidation.
- exact totals: integer cents/bigint, atomic row increments, recompute from source for repairs; no approximate or cached aggregates.
- bounded write overhead: constant indexed row writes per order operation.

## Alternatives considered
### Direct optimized source query
- add indexes, covering indexes, maybe materialized aggregates. But joins/sorting over 3M rows and exact totals remain expensive; cannot guarantee p95 under all filters; write amplification not solved.
### Database triggers / stored procedures
- Same atomcity, but logic in SQL hidden, hard to test, language mismatch, less maintainable. App hooks chosen with same transaction and integration tests.
### Asynchronous CDC / change data capture
- Pros: decoupled, replay, scalable. Cons: eventual consistency; consumer lag means approve not visible on next request; infra (broker, connectors, monitoring); idempotency/ordering; exact totals possible but latency. If made synchronous by waiting for projection, request blocks on external system and becomes fragile; no p95 guarantee.
### Event sourcing / event store with projections
- Could provide replay and audit, but requires changing source of truth, event schemas, handlers, snapshots; async consumers introduce same lag; synchronous projection handling is effectively app-level hook with more ceremony. Existing transactional order tables already provide audit via updated_at and history? Actually no history but okay. Overkill.
### Materialized views / scheduled batch refresh
- PG matviews can speed reads but refresh is costly; full refresh locks, concurrent refresh builds temp table and requires unique index; per-write refresh in transaction not practical; schedule leaves gap violating read-your-writes; aggregate matview per company/status may work but row-level operations list still needs denormalization. Exact totals via aggregate matview possible but refresh interval problem; concurrent high writes lead to stale aggregates.
### ETL/data warehouse or separate cache
- Adds infra and consistency problems; exact financial totals and immediate reads require synchronous propagation; not justified.

## Consistency and failure model
- same-transaction maintenance: if projection fails, source write rolls back; no partial visibility. If crash before commit, none. After commit, both visible.
- Residual divergence from bugs/manual edits/skipped historical rows handled by re-derivation and drift repair.
- Idempotent: upsert by order id; deterministic rebuild; totals recomputed from corrected rows not incremental deltas after corruption.
- Concurrency: row-level locks and atomic increments on totals row; each status change adjusts old/new contributions; final exact regardless of interleaving.
- Scheduled drift repair every 5 minutes (or manual window) bounds detection time for anomalies; arbitrary window re-derivation supports large corrections/backfills.

## Trade-offs accepted
- coupling writes to projection correctness; mitigated by tests (RYOW, concurrent totals, drift repair), rebuild routine.
- write latency slightly higher; acceptable relative to dashboard p95 requirement and write volume.
- no multi-instance CDC scalability initially; if write throughput grows, could introduce CDC but would need to preserve RYOW via synchronous path or accept different SLA.

## Conclusion
- sync hooks are lowest-complexity design satisfying immediate visibility and exact totals while achieving fast reads; re-derivation/drift repair provide recovery.

# Design

## Requirements driving the design
The operations dashboard lists derived rows from payment orders, events, and workers. It must remain fast at ~3M source orders: p95 under 50ms, with filters by company, status, and date range, sorted by recency and paginated. Operators must read their own writes immediately after a source write commits, for example an approval appearing on the next dashboard request. Per-company financial totals must be exact, not approximate or eventually converging after a visible delay.

## Chosen approach
Use synchronous, application-managed read models maintained in the same database transaction as the source write.

The design keeps `payment_orders` and related reference tables as the system of record. It adds derived read models:
- a per-operation row containing the fields needed by the dashboard, denormalized so the read path does not join payment orders with events and workers;
- a per-company totals row containing exact financial aggregates.

The dashboard query reads only the per-operation read model. The row model is indexed for the dominant access patterns: company plus status plus recency, and company plus recency without a status filter. This turns the expensive multi-table join and sort over millions of rows into an indexed single-table page fetch.

Write services invoke projection maintenance hooks inside the same transaction as their source updates:
- order creation inserts/updates the operation row and increases the company's pending contribution;
- approval or rejection updates the operation row's status and moves the amount between exact total columns while adjusting pending counts.

Because the source change and read-model change commit together, a successful write is immediately visible to the next dashboard query. There is no background propagation window and no cache invalidation step.

The design also includes recovery facilities: a re-derivation routine for an arbitrary date window and a scheduled drift-repair job. These make the system self-healing if a projection row is missing, stale, manually edited, or affected by an unforeseen bug.

## Why synchronous hooks satisfy the requirements
...

Alternative sections:

### Directly optimizing the source query
Adding indexes, covering indexes, or partial indexes can reduce latency but does not remove fundamental cost: the dashboard filters/sorts over 3M orders and joins reference tables; financial totals require aggregating many rows. Indexes can help, but p95 under 50ms across all filters and pagination would be fragile. Projection precomputes the read shape at write time.

### Database triggers or stored procedures
Triggers can provide same transactional atomcity. They were not chosen because they move business-visible behavior into SQL, making it harder to test in TypeScript, harder to version with application code, and harder to reason about during migrations. Application-level hooks keep validation, transaction orchestration, and tests in the same stack while still being transactional.

### Change data capture / async replication
CDC can watch source table changes and update projections in a consumer. It is attractive for decoupling and replay, but it introduces an asynchronous pipeline. Even with low-latency connectors, the projection may lag behind the committed source row. That violates the requirement that an approval be visible on the next request unless the API blocks until the consumer has applied the change, which adds network dependency and makes write latency depend on external infrastructure. CDC also increases operational surface: connector health, message ordering, idempotent consumers, backpressure, and exactly-once semantics. For this requirement, those costs buy durability/replay capabilities that the re-derivation and drift-repair routines already provide more simply.

### Event sourcing / event-driven projections
Event sourcing would make events the source of truth and build dashboards by replaying or consuming them. If projection processing is asynchronous, it has the same read-your-writes lag as CDC. If it is synchronous inside the same transaction, it is largely equivalent to application-level projection hooks but with much higher complexity: immutable event schema, event store integration, handler idempotence, snapshots, and migration of existing order workflows. Since the source tables already provide transactional records and the task is to improve a read path, event sourcing is disproportionate.

### Materialized views
PostgreSQL materialized views can precompute the read shape, but they do not naturally solve immediate read-your-writes. Refreshing a materialized view is a separate operation. Full refresh can take locks; concurrent refresh builds new data and swaps it in, which is expensive if done frequently. Synchronously refreshing the view on every write would create long transactions and lock contention, defeating the performance goal. A schedule leaves a staleness window. A materialized aggregate for totals might be exact after refresh, but the same staleness applies to operators viewing their just-approved orders.

### Separate cache or data warehouse
A cache can be fast but must handle invalidation immediately after writes. A warehouse is typically batch-oriented and unsuitable for exact, immediate operational financial totals. Both add infrastructure without providing the simpler all-or-nothing transactional guarantee needed here.

## Consistency, concurrency, and recovery
- All-or-nothing: source write and projection maintenance commit or roll back together. A failed projection update cannot leave a visible source row without its read-model counterpart.
- Read-your-writes: after commit, the next query reads the committed projection row. No lag, no invalidation event.
- Exact totals: amounts are integral and stored as big integers. Total adjustments use atomic database operations on the company totals row, so concurrent approvals for the same company do not lose updates. The same-order transition check is also guarded to prevent double transitions under concurrency.
- Idempotent repair: re-derivation can rebuild a window from the source tables; drift repair compares source and projection for a window, upserts missing/stale rows, removes orphans, and recalculates affected totals. The scheduled job bounds the time any residual divergence can persist; manual re-derivation supports larger corrections or backfills.
- Reference data: denormalized event and worker fields are copied when the order row is written. If reference data changes outside the specified write path, the re-derivation/drift-repair routines can refresh affected windows.

## Trade-offs accepted
The main trade-off is coupling the write path to projection maintenance. If a hook has a bug, writes can fail or read models can drift. This is accepted because the requirement prioritizes immediate consistency and exact totals over loose coupling. The risk is mitigated by transactional failures, integration tests for read-your-writes and concurrent totals, drift repair, and window re-derivation. Write latency increases modestly due to a small number of indexed row updates, but this is acceptable relative to removing a 20-30 second dashboard query and meeting the 50ms read target.

If future write volume makes the synchronous projection too expensive, CDC could be reconsidered, but it would need to preserve the read-your-writes SLA or accept a different consistency contract.

## Conclusion
Synchronous in-transaction projection hooks are the lowest-complexity design that simultaneously provides a fast indexed read model, immediate operator visibility of writes, exact company financial totals, and a practical recovery story. CDC, event sourcing, materialized views, and pure source-query optimization either introduce unacceptable staleness, operational complexity, or refresh costs for the stated requirements.

## reply

```markdown
# Design

## Requirements driving the design

The operations dashboard lists derived rows from payment orders, events, and workers. It must remain fast at roughly three million source orders: p95 under 50 ms, with filters by company, status, and date range, sorted by recency and paginated. Operators must read their own writes immediately after a source write commits — for example, an approval should be visible on the next dashboard request. Per-company financial totals must be exact, not approximate or eventually converging after a visible delay.

## Chosen approach

Use synchronous, application-managed read models maintained in the same database transaction as the source write.

The design keeps payment orders and related reference tables as the system of record. It adds derived read models:

- a per-operation row containing the fields needed by the dashboard, denormalized so the read path does not join payment orders with events and workers;
- a per-company totals row containing exact financial aggregates.

The dashboard query reads only the per-operation read model. The read model is indexed for the dominant access patterns: company plus status plus recency, and company plus recency without a status filter. This turns the expensive multi-table join and sort over millions of rows into an indexed single-table page fetch.

Write services invoke projection maintenance hooks inside the same transaction as their source updates:

- order creation inserts or updates the operation row and increases the company's pending contribution;
- approval or rejection updates the operation row's status and moves the amount between exact total columns while adjusting pending counts.

Because the source change and read-model change commit together, a successful write is immediately visible to the next dashboard query. There is no background propagation window and no cache invalidation step.

The design also includes recovery facilities: a re-derivation routine for an arbitrary date window and a scheduled drift-repair job. These make the system self-healing if a projection row is missing, stale, manually edited, or affected by an unforeseen bug.

## Why synchronous hooks satisfy the requirements

### Fast reads

The dashboard no longer computes a join across payment orders, events, and workers on every request. It reads a narrow, precomputed table whose indexes match the dashboard filters and sort order. Pagination and filtered counts are served from the same read model, which makes the 50 ms p95 target realistic even with millions of source orders.

### Immediate read-your-writes

The projection is updated before the transaction commits. A reader that queries after the commit sees both the source state and the read-model state. This avoids the central weakness of asynchronous pipelines: there is no consumer lag between "the approval was written" and "the approval appears on the dashboard."

### Exact financial totals

Totals are maintained as exact integer values, not floating-point aggregates or approximate counters. The company totals row is updated with atomic row-level operations inside the write transaction. This avoids lost updates when multiple operators approve or reject orders for the same company concurrently. Recovery routines can also recompute affected totals from the corrected read model, so accumulated drift is not allowed to persist.

### Bounded write overhead

Each write performs a small number of indexed row updates: the source row, the operation read-model row, and the company totals row. This is constant per operation and does not grow with table size. The added write latency is modest and is the acceptable cost of making reads fast and consistent.

## Alternatives considered

### Directly optimizing the source query

Adding indexes, covering indexes, or partial indexes can reduce query time, but it does not remove the fundamental shape of the problem: the dashboard filters, sorts, and paginates over millions of source rows while joining reference tables. Financial totals would still require aggregation over large ranges. Optimizations may help, but they make the 50 ms target fragile and do not solve read-your-writes. The projection precomputes the read shape at write time, which is a better fit for the requirement.

### Database triggers or stored procedures

Triggers could provide the same transactional atomcity and would keep projection maintenance very close to the data. They were not chosen because they move business-visible behavior into SQL, making it harder to test in TypeScript, harder to version alongside application code, and harder to reason about during migrations. Application-level hooks keep validation, transaction orchestration, and tests in the same stack while still committing source and projection changes together.

### Change data capture or asynchronous replication

CDC can watch source-table changes and update projections in a consumer. It is attractive for decoupling, replayability, and horizontal scaling, but it introduces an asynchronous pipeline. Even with low-latency connectors, the projection may lag behind the committed source row. That violates the requirement that an approval be visible on the next request unless the API blocks until the consumer has applied the change. Blocking would make write latency depend on external infrastructure and would remove the simple all-or-nothing transactional guarantee.

CDC also increases operational surface: connector health, message ordering, idempotent consumers, backpressure, monitoring, and exactly-once semantics. For this requirement, those costs buy capabilities that re-derivation and drift repair already provide more simply.

### Event sourcing or event-driven projections

Event sourcing would make events the source of truth and build dashboards by consuming or replaying them. If projection processing is asynchronous, it has the same read-your-writes lag as CDC. If it is synchronous inside the same transaction, it is largely equivalent to application-level projection hooks but with much higher complexity: immutable event schemas, event store integration, handler idempotence, snapshots, and migration of existing order workflows.

Since the source tables already provide transactional records and the task is to improve a read path, event sourcing is disproportionate. The design still gets a useful part of that idea — bounded rebuilds through re-derivation and drift repair — without changing the system of record.

### Materialized views

PostgreSQL materialized views can precompute the read shape, but they do not naturally solve immediate read-your-writes. Refreshing a materialized view is a separate operation. Full refresh can take locks; concurrent refresh builds new data and swaps it in, which is expensive if done frequently. Synchronously refreshing the view on every write would create long transactions and lock contention, defeating the performance goal. A schedule leaves a staleness window.

A materialized aggregate for totals might be exact after refresh, but the same staleness applies to operators viewing their just-approved orders. Materialized views are therefore a poor fit for the combination of immediate visibility, exact totals, and low read latency.

### Separate cache or data warehouse

A cache can be fast but must handle invalidation immediately after writes. A warehouse is typically batch-oriented and unsuitable for exact, immediate operational financial totals. Both add infrastructure without providing the simpler transactional guarantee needed here.

## Consistency, concurrency, and recovery

- All-or-nothing writes: the source write and projection maintenance commit or roll back together. A failed projection update cannot leave a visible source row without its read-model counterpart.
- Read-your-writes: after commit, the next query reads the committed projection row. There is no propagation delay and no invalidation event.
- Exact totals: amounts are integral and stored as large integers. Total adjustments use atomic database operations on the company totals row, so concurrent updates for the same company do not lose contributions.
- Safe transitions: order status changes are validated inside the write transaction and guarded so concurrent transitions for the same order cannot both succeed incorrectly.
- Idempotent repair: re-derivation can rebuild a date window from the source tables. Drift repair compares source and projection for a window, upserts missing or stale rows, removes orphans, and recalculates affected totals.
- Bounded drift detection: the scheduled drift-repair job limits how long residual divergence can persist. Manual re-derivation supports larger corrections or backfills.
- Reference data: denormalized event and worker fields are copied when the order row is written. If reference data changes outside the specified write path, the re-derivation and drift-repair routines can refresh affected windows.

## Trade-offs accepted

The main trade-off is coupling the write path to projection maintenance. If a hook has a bug, writes can fail or read models can drift. This is accepted because the requirement prioritizes immediate consistency and exact totals over loose coupling. The risk is mitigated by transactional failure semantics, integration tests for read-your-writes and concurrent totals, drift repair, and window re-derivation.

Write latency increases modestly because each source write also updates a few indexed projection rows. That cost is acceptable relative to removing a 20–30 second dashboard query and meeting the 50 ms read target.

If future write volume makes the synchronous projection too expensive, CDC could be reconsidered, but it would need to preserve the read-your-writes SLA or accept a different consistency contract.

## Conclusion

Synchronous in-transaction projection hooks are the lowest-complexity design that simultaneously provides a fast indexed read model, immediate operator visibility of writes, exact company financial totals, and a practical recovery story. CDC, event sourcing, materialized views, and pure source-query optimization either introduce unacceptable staleness, operational complexity, or refresh costs for the stated requirements.
```

import { Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Cron, CronExpression } from '@nestjs/schedule';

import { ProjectionsService } from '../projections/projections.service';
import type { DriftReport } from '../projections/projections.types';

const DEFAULT_WINDOW_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000; // last 1 hour

@Injectable()
export class DriftRepairProcessor {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(DriftRepairProcessor.name);

  constructor(private readonly projections: ProjectionsService) {}

  @Cron(CronExpression.EVERY_5_MINUTES)
  async run(): Promise<void> {
    const to = new Date();
    const from = new Date(to.getTime() - DEFAULT_WINDOW_MS);
    const report: DriftReport = await this.runForWindow(from, to);
    this.logger.log(
      `drift repair complete: window=${from.toISOString()}..${to.toISOString()} rowsCorrected=${report.rowsCorrected} totalsCorrected=${report.totalsCorrected}`,
    );
  }

  /** Manual trigger; window defaults to last 1 hour. */
  async runForWindow(from: Date, to: Date): Promise<DriftReport> {
    return this.projections.repairDrift(from, to);
  }
}
```

import { Injectable, BadRequestException, NotFoundException } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ProjectionsRepository } from './projections.repository';
import {
  CreateOrderInput,
  OrderStatus,
  OperationRow,
  CompanyTotals,
  DriftReport,
} from './projections.types';

@Injectable()
export class ProjectionsService {
  constructor(private readonly repo: ProjectionsRepository) {}

  async applyOrderCreated(
    input: CreateOrderInput,
    order: { id: string; createdAt: Date },
  ): Promise<void> {
    const row = await this.repo.fetchSourceRow(order.id);
    if (!row) {
      throw new NotFoundException({
        error: {
          code: 'order_not_found',
          message: `Order ${order.id} not found in source`,
          details: { orderId: order.id },
        },
      });
    }
    await this.repo.upsertOrder(row);
    await this.repo.adjustTotals(input.companyId, { pendingDelta: 1 });
  }

  async applyOrderStatusChanged(
    orderId: string,
    newStatus: OrderStatus,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const row = await this.repo.fetchSourceRow(orderId);
    if (!row) {
      throw new NotFoundException({
        error: {
          code: 'order_not_found',
          message: `Order ${orderId} not found in source`,
          details: { orderId },
        },
      });
    }
    await this.repo.updateOrderStatus(orderId, newStatus);
    
    const delta: { approvedCents?: bigint; rejectedCents?: bigint; pendingDelta?: number } = {};
    if (newStatus === 'approved') {
      delta.pendingDelta = -1;
      delta.approvedCents = BigInt(row.amountCents);
    } else if (newStatus === 'rejected') {
      delta.pendingDelta = -1;
      delta.rejectedCents = BigInt(row.amountCents);
    }
    await this.repo.adjustTotals(row.companyId, delta);
  }

  async rederive(from: Date, to: Date): Promise<DriftReport> {
    const rows = await this.repo.fetchSourceWindow(from, to);
    await this.repo.deleteProjectionWindow(from, to);
    await this.repo.bulkUpsert(rows);

    // Recompute totals for affected companies
    const companyMap = new Map<string, { approved: bigint; rejected: bigint; pending: number }>();
    for (const row of rows) {
      const entry = companyMap.get(row.companyId) ?? { approved: 0n, rejected: 0n, pending: 0 };
      if (row.status === 'approved') {
        entry.approved += BigInt(row.amountCents);
      } else if (row.status === 'rejected') {
        entry.rejected += BigInt(row.amountCents);
      } else if (row.status === 'pending') {
        entry.pending += 1;
      }
      companyMap.set(row.companyId, entry);
    }

  async repairDrift(from: Date, to: Date): Promise<DriftReport> {
    const sourceRows = await this.repo.fetchSourceWindow(from, to);
    const projectionRows = await this.repo.fetchProjectionWindow(from, to);

    const sourceMap = new Map(sourceRows.map(r => [r.id, r]));
    const projectionMap = new Map(projectionRows.map(r => [r.id, r]));

import { Injectable, NotFoundException } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ProjectionsRepository } from './projections.repository';
import {
  CreateOrderInput,
  OrderStatus,
  OperationRow,
  CompanyTotals,
  DriftReport,
} from './projections.types';

@Injectable()
export class ProjectionsService {
  constructor(private readonly repo: ProjectionsRepository) {}

  async applyOrderCreated(

    if (!row) {

    }

    await this.repo.adjustTotals(input.companyId, { pendingDelta: 1 });
  }

  async applyOrderStatusChanged(
    orderId: string,

  ): Promise<void> {
    const row = await this.repo.fetchSourceRow(orderId);
    if (!row) {
      throw new NotFoundException({
        error: {
          code: 'order_not_found',
          message: `Order ${orderId} not found in source`,
          details: { orderId },
        },
      });
    }

    await this.repo.updateOrderStatus(orderId, newStatus);

    const delta: {
      approvedCents?: bigint;
      rejectedCents?: bigint;
      pendingDelta?: number;
    } = {};

    if (newStatus === 'approved') {
      delta.pendingDelta = -1;
      delta.approvedCents = BigInt(row.amountCents);
    } else if (newStatus === 'rejected') {
      delta.pendingDelta = -1;
      delta.rejectedCents = BigInt(row.amountCents);
    }

    await this.repo.adjustTotals(row.companyId, delta);

  // calling resetTotals. This yields correct all-time totals when rederive covers the full
  // history for the affected companies. For a partial window it would overwrite all-time
  // totals with window-only values; the plan prescribes this behaviour explicitly.
  async rederive(from: Date, to: Date): Promise<DriftReport> {
    const rows = await this.repo.fetchSourceWindow(from, to);

    await this.repo.deleteProjectionWindow(from, to);
    if (rows.length > 0) {
      await this.repo.bulkUpsert(rows);
    }

    const companyMap = new Map<
      string,
      { approved: bigint; rejected: bigint; pending: number }
    >();

    for (const row of rows) {
      const entry =
        companyMap.get(row.companyId) ?? { approved: 0n, rejected: 0n, pending: 0 };
      if (row.status === 'approved') {
        entry.approved += BigInt(row.amountCents);
      } else if (row.status === 'rejected') {
        entry.rejected += BigInt(row.amountCents);
      } else if (row.status === 'pending') {
        entry.pending += 1;
      }
      companyMap.set(row.companyId, entry);
    }

    for (const [companyId, totals] of companyMap) {
      await this.repo.resetTotals(companyId, {
        companyId,
        approvedTotalCents: totals.approved,
        rejectedTotalCents: totals.rejected,
        pendingCount: totals.pending,
      });
    }

    return {
      windowStart: from,
      windowEnd: to,
      rowsCorrected: rows.length,
      totalsCorrected: companyMap.size > 0,
    };
  }

  async repairDrift(from: Date, to: Date): Promise<DriftReport> {
    const sourceRows = await this.repo.fetchSourceWindow(from, to);
    const projectionRows = await this.repo.fetchProjectionWindow(from, to);

    const sourceMap = new Map(sourceRows.map((r) => [r.id, r]));
    const projectionMap = new Map(projectionRows.map((r) => [r.id, r]));

    const rowsToUpsert: OperationRow[] = [];
    for (const [id, srcRow] of sourceMap) {

      if (!projRow || this.rowsDiffer(srcRow, projRow)) {
        rowsToUpsert.push(srcRow);
      }

        windowEnd: to,
        rowsCorrected: 0,
        totalsCorrected: false,

    if (sourceRows.length > 0) {

    // Adjust totals by the delta between old projection contribution and new source contribution.
    const affectedCompanies = new Set<string>();
    sourceRows.forEach((r) => affectedCompanies.add(r.companyId));
    projectionRows.forEach((r) => affectedCompanies.add(r.companyId));

      const deltaRejected = newContrib.rejected - oldContrib.rejected;
      const deltaPending = newContrib.pending - oldContrib.pending;

      if (deltaApproved !== 0n || deltaRejected !== 0n || deltaPending !== 0) {
        await this.repo.adjustTotals(companyId, {
          approvedCents: deltaApproved !== 0n ? deltaApproved : undefined,
          rejectedCents: deltaRejected !== 0n ? deltaRejected : undefined,
          pendingDelta: deltaPending !== 0 ? deltaPending : undefined,
        });
        totalsCorrected = true;
      }
    }

    return {
      windowStart: from,
      windowEnd: to,
      rowsCorrected: rowsToUpsert.length + orphanedCount,
      totalsCorrected,
    };
  }

  async getTotals(companyId: string): Promise<CompanyTotals> {
    const totals = await this.repo.getTotals(companyId);
    if (!totals) {
      throw new NotFoundException({
        error: {
          code: 'company_not_found',
          message: `No totals found for company ${companyId}`,
          details: { companyId },
        },
      });
    }
    return totals;
  }

  private rowsDiffer(a: OperationRow, b: OperationRow): boolean {
    return (
      a.status !== b.status ||
      a.amountCents !== b.amountCents ||
      a.workerName !== b.workerName ||
      a.eventTitle !== b.eventTitle ||
      a.eventLocation !== b.eventLocation
    );
  }

  private computeContribution(
    rows: OperationRow[],
  ): { approved: bigint; rejected: bigint; pending: number } {
    let approved = 0n;
    let rejected = 0n;
    let pending = 0;
    for (const row of rows) {
      if (row.status === 'approved') approved += BigInt(row.amountCents);
      else if (row.status === 'rejected') rejected += BigInt(row.amountCents);
      else if (row.status === 'pending') pending++;
    }
    return { approved, rejected, pending };
  }
}
```

import { Injectable, NotFoundException, BadRequestException } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';
import { ProjectionsService } from '../projections/projections.service';
import { CreateOrderInput, OrderStatus } from '../projections/projections.types';

@Injectable()
export class WritesService {
  constructor(
    private readonly prisma: PrismaClient,
    private readonly projections: ProjectionsService,
  ) {}

  async createOrder(input: CreateOrderInput): Promise<{ id: string; status: OrderStatus }> {
    const result = await this.prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
      const order = await tx.paymentOrder.create({
        data: {
          companyId: input.companyId,
          workerId: input.workerId,
          eventId: input.eventId,
          amountCents: input.amountCents,
          status: 'pending',
        },
      });

      await this.projections.applyOrderCreated(input, {
        id: order.id,
        createdAt: order.createdAt,
      });

      return { id: order.id, status: order.status };
    });

    return result;
  }

  async approveOrder(orderId: string): Promise<{ id: string; status: OrderStatus }> {
    return this.changeOrderStatus(orderId, 'approved');
  }

  async rejectOrder(orderId: string): Promise<{ id: string; status: OrderStatus }> {
    return this.changeOrderStatus(orderId, 'rejected');
  }

  private async changeOrderStatus(orderId: string, newStatus: OrderStatus): Promise<{ id: string; status: OrderStatus }> {
    return this.prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
      const order = await tx.paymentOrder.findUnique({
        where: { id: orderId },
      });

      if (!order) {
        throw new NotFoundException('Order not found');
      }

      if (order.status === newStatus) {
        throw new BadRequestException('Invalid transition');
      }

      await tx.paymentOrder.update({
        where: { id: orderId },
        data: { status: newStatus },
      });

      await this.projections.applyOrderStatusChanged(orderId, newStatus);

      return { id: order.id, status: newStatus };
    });
  }
}

    return this.prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
      const order = await tx.paymentOrder.create({
        data: {
          companyId: input.companyId,
          workerId: input.workerId,
          eventId: input.eventId,
          amountCents: input.amountCents,
        },
      });

      await this.projections.applyOrderCreated(input, {
        id: order.id,
        createdAt: order.createdAt,
      });

      return { id: order.id, status: order.status };
    });
  }

  async approveOrder(orderId: string): Promise<{ id: string; status: OrderStatus }> {
    return this.changeOrderStatus(orderId, 'approved');
  }

  async rejectOrder(orderId: string): Promise<{ id: string; status: OrderStatus }> {
    return this.changeOrderStatus(orderId, 'rejected');
  }

  private async changeOrderStatus(
    orderId: string,
    newStatus: OrderStatus,
  ): Promise<{ id: string; status: OrderStatus }> {

      const order = await tx.paymentOrder.findUnique({
        where: { id: orderId },
      });

      if (!order) {
        throw new NotFoundException(`Order ${orderId} not found`);
      }

      if (order.status === newStatus) {
        throw new BadRequestException(`Invalid transition: order is already ${newStatus}`);
      }

      await tx.paymentOrder.update({
        where: { id: orderId },
        data: { status: newStatus },
      });

      await this.projections.applyOrderStatusChanged(orderId, newStatus);

      return { id: order.id, status: newStatus };

  }
}
